decision.question: How does one card opt in to tiny tabs?
options: a {"layout": "tabs"} data line in the card's page.jsonl, read as this.layout
a new verb method on Card (layout())
decision.why: core's set() already keeps an unknown key as data, so card.js needs no new verb, and no other card can change

decision.question: Where does the open tab live?
options: #tab=<name> in the url, pushState per click
decision.chose: #tab=<name>, with localStorage as the fallback when the url names none
decision.why: a hash never re-routes the page; one history entry per tab makes Back step through tabs

decision.question: How does the chat become a tab?
options: CSS :has() on the tab strip's data-tab hides or shows the existing .ai2-foot
move the chat into the panel in JS
decision.why: the chat keeps its live connection and composer; nothing is rebuilt

log.msg: Kept the card's title row (title, cost, Actions) above the strip: it names the card, it is not a section. The ai2- prefix is not reserved in css-scopes.txt; that file is outside this fence (line to add: ai2-   /framework/ai2). No readme/doc edit: ai2/readme.md and doc/ are outside the fence. No separate walkthrough page: the outcome's shots, one per tab, are the walkthrough.

decision.question: How is each tab a real page without a folder?
options: core route(): Card.route(name) builds a Page per tab on demand, mounted in the card's regions panel (core's claim for a named child, as ext/tabs does)
a folder and page.jsonl per tab (the mastermind's first ruling, withdrawn by the owner)
decision.why: the owner: dynamic routed pages through the page route mechanism, no directory yet. core/Page is unchanged; no folders were created and no lines were moved.

decision.question: Can a tab path collide with a request (sub-card) path?
options: the request keeps its name, the tab becomes <name>-tab
decision.why: route() is only tried for undeclared names and Card.child() checks the requests first, so a request can never be shadowed; the rename keeps the tab reachable. The owner's example shape /now/usage/ holds.

decision.question: Where does the tab padding come from?
options: a {"tab_classes": "pad"} line on the Now card, the framework's own .pad
pad by default on every tiny tab page
decision.chose: the line on the Now card
decision.why: the owner: padding is not a default, it should not have to be fought off. Other cards get no padding from this.

log.msg: Removed the hash routing, the popstate listener and localStorage for tiny cards: the routed child page is the one source of the open tab. Fixed a 60px flow gap above each tab body (the hidden page title left a * + * margin).
